claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is equiatomic.
The initial Co-free alloy is an as-solidified, homogeneous polycrystalline solid solution.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi changes the intrinsic stacking-fault energy.
The stacking-fault energy governs the balance between dislocation slip and deformation twinning in the Co-free alloy.
The Co-induced change in stacking-fault energy promotes a temperature- and strain-rate-dependent transition from dislocation slip to deformation twinning.
Lower temperature and higher strain rate favor twin nucleation over dislocation slip in the Co-free alloy.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation promotes dislocation glide.
Thermally activated dislocation glide at higher temperatures diminishes deformation twinning.
The transition toward deformation twinning enhances strain hardening at lower temperatures and high strain rates relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
The transition toward deformation twinning enhances ductility at lower temperatures and high strain rates relative to CoCrFeMnNi.
The Co-free alloy will have significantly higher twin density than CoCrFeMnNi at low temperatures and high strain rates.
The higher predicted twin density will be associated with enhanced strain hardening.
Differences in deformation mechanism between the Co-free and Co-containing alloys will diminish as temperature increases.
Differences in strain-rate sensitivity between the Co-free and Co-containing alloys will diminish as temperature increases.
The proposed mechanism applies from room temperature to approximately 600 °C and from 10^-4 to 10^0 s^-1.
Additional deformation mechanisms may prevail outside the specified temperature and strain-rate bounds.
